plan.architecture_summary: `bat` is a Rust command-line tool that acts as a `cat` clone with syntax highlighting, Git integration, and automatic paging. Its codebase is structured around a core library in `src/` (with modules for configuration, parsing, printing, syntax mapping, and terminal handling) and a binary entry point in `src/bin/bat/`. Integration and syntax tests reside under the `tests/` directory. Building and testing are managed via standard Cargo commands.

Regression tests are strongly encouraged under tests/integration_tests.rs.

issues.title: --list-themes + BAT_OPTS can be problematic
issues.why: Labeled 'good first issue' and involves small configuration/CLI handling adjustments in Rust.
issues.approach: Investigate how `--list-themes` handles config and pagination, and adjust settings or ignore paging when listing themes. Add a regression test for running `--list-themes` with custom options.

issues.title: Custom fallback syntax opt-in
issues.why: A great beginner issue for exploring CLI option parsing and config defaults in `bat`.
issues.approach: Examine how fallback syntax can be specified or configured as an opt-in setting in the CLI app parser and config. Verify behavior with existing integration tests.

issues.title: --wrap unpaged
issues.why: A feature request allowing a beginner to dive into wrapping logic and configuration parsing.
issues.approach: Examine how `--wrap` mode can be configured or updated for unpaged vs paged output according to user requirements.

first_timer_insights: First-time PRs typically touch `src/`, add or update regression tests in `tests/integration_tests.rs`, and include an entry in `CHANGELOG.md`.
caveats: No explicit pre-commit hook scripts or linting commands were found in the config files beyond standard cargo/rustfmt.
